questions.q: What does Epictetus say life's hardships are for?
a: They push us to grow into stronger people
They reveal which friends are loyal
They balance out the good times
They test whether we deserve success
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that without obstacles, like Hercules without labours, we would never strive to improve.

questions.q: What point does Epictetus make with the example of grapes and figs?
a: Greatness develops slowly and cannot be rushed
Some people ripen faster than others
Hard work always produces a harvest
Patience matters more than talent
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a fruit must blossom, bear fruit, and ripen, so no great thing happens overnight.

questions.q: According to the Stoic principle in the summary, what should you focus your energy on?
a: How you respond to what happens
Preventing bad events from occurring
Changing the minds of other people
Avoiding situations you cannot predict
questions.why: Lesson 3 says external events are outside our control, but our reaction to them is where responsibility lies.

questions.q: Where does the summary say good and evil actually exist?
a: In our mind and our will
In the events that happen to us
In the opinions of society
In the hands of fate
questions.why: Lesson 3 concludes that good and evil exist only in our mind and will, not in outside circumstances.

questions.q: What goes wrong when you confuse what you can and cannot control?
a: You waste effort on things outside your power
You become overly confident in your choices
You stop caring about other people
You lose interest in long-term goals
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that mixing up the two makes you react to what you cannot change and neglect what matters.
